records.title: Simulations and robots
records.summary: Use models, software and machines to make a specific human task easier, safer or better understood. This broad strand connects care and hospitality with creative worlds, scientific observation and ambitious infrastructure. The twenty original suggestions are different starting points, not one product roadmap.

records.title: Clean power systems
records.summary: Begin with the energy service people need: a reliable home, a working workshop, useful heat, transport or clean water. The ten original suggestions include established engineering pathways and frontier research. Each needs its own evidence, customer and complete accounting of inputs and outputs.

records.title: Closed-loop food
records.summary: Connect food people enjoy with reliable production, useful livelihoods and careful use of materials. The ten original themes span familiar crops, seafood, fungi, insects and scientific research. A loop is a design question: its inputs, outputs, losses and responsibilities still need to be measured.

records.title: Waste reclamation
records.summary: Keep useful products and materials in service by matching a specific stream to a real need. The ten original suggestions range from computer repair and farm residues to specialised industrial and nuclear research questions. They require different expertise and must not be treated as interchangeable recovery opportunities.

records.title: Subterranean cities
records.summary: Use a bold habitat vision to ask concrete questions about a life people would choose, the services it depends on and who decides its future. The ten original themes include preservation, excavation, maintenance, production, transport, life support, governance and entertainment. City-scale feasibility remains unproven.

records.title: Extreme metamaterials
records.summary: Materials shape what an invention can do, how long it lasts and whether it can be repaired. This category brings together polymers, ceramics, crystals, electrodes, optics and more demanding research ambitions. Its starting discipline is simple: name the property, identify the sample and measure it under conditions that matter. A striking material image or an extreme title is an invitation to investigate, not proof of a breakthrough.

records.title: Space industry
records.summary: Space enterprises connect human needs with unforgiving engineering questions. This category spans inclusive spacewear, radiation research, fabrication, large payloads, long-duration habitats and openly speculative travel ideas. The scale of the vision is welcome, but every project needs a clear account of what can be tested on Earth, what depends on a future mission and what remains a question in fundamental science.

records.title: Micro-architectures
records.summary: Small devices can create large possibilities, from an ordinary sensor that saves a worker time to a frontier experiment about quantum information. This category connects electronics, chip design, fluid systems, near-eye displays and molecular or programmable-matter ideas. Each entry should explain its mechanism, inputs, outputs and evidence before asking readers to accept a future application.

records.title: Humanities and fun
records.summary: A good future needs stories, pleasure, learning, friendship and room to ask difficult questions. These enterprises connect creative work with everyday wellbeing and the ways people choose to live together. Some can begin as a small production or learning circle. Others, such as radical life extension, belong to research and should never be presented as a ready-made personal benefit.

records.title: Market analysis
records.summary: A market is made of people, routines, institutions and unmet needs, not just a large number in a pitch deck. This category investigates care, learning, wellbeing, migration, disruption, food, housing, population change and governance. Its purpose is to discover a useful service question with the people affected, then test whether a proposed enterprise can answer it.

records.title: Aura of Intelligence
records.summary: Aura brings the network's questions about intelligence, identity, assistance and responsibility into everyday life. The ideas range from the Queens framework and public art to personal interfaces, inclusive apparel and participant-led care tools. Consciousness remains a philosophical and research question. A persona, mirror or generated response is not evidence that a system is conscious.

categories.title: Simulations and robots
categories.summary: Use models, software and machines to make a specific human task easier, safer or better understood. This broad strand connects care and hospitality with creative worlds, scientific observation and ambitious infrastructure. The twenty original suggestions are different starting points, not one product roadmap.
sharedInfrastructure: A shared simulation and data workspace with source records, units, assumptions and version history.
Accessible prototype facilities where different bodies, communication styles and levels of technical experience can participate.
Human mentors in robotics, operations, care and science who review the boundary between a demonstration and a deployable service.

categories.title: Clean power systems
categories.summary: Begin with the energy service people need: a reliable home, a working workshop, useful heat, transport or clean water. The ten original suggestions include established engineering pathways and frontier research. Each needs its own evidence, customer and complete accounting of inputs and outputs.
sharedInfrastructure: A common load-data and comparison method, with the same service requirement applied to every option.
Qualified electrical, mechanical, water and marine advice appropriate to the specific proposal.
A service and maintenance knowledge base that records spare parts, response times, training and whole-life responsibilities.

categories.title: Closed-loop food
categories.summary: Connect food people enjoy with reliable production, useful livelihoods and careful use of materials. The ten original themes span familiar crops, seafood, fungi, insects and scientific research. A loop is a design question: its inputs, outputs, losses and responsibilities still need to be measured.
sharedInfrastructure: A shared product-brief format covering the customer, ingredient provenance, quality requirements, handling and repeat demand.
Access to qualified food-development, production and laboratory partners for the chosen application.
A producer-and-buyer coordination service that distinguishes forecasts from confirmed orders and records the complete labour and material balance.

categories.title: Waste reclamation
categories.summary: Keep useful products and materials in service by matching a specific stream to a real need. The ten original suggestions range from computer repair and farm residues to specialised industrial and nuclear research questions. They require different expertise and must not be treated as interchangeable recovery opportunities.
sharedInfrastructure: A material register recording source, ownership, composition, contamination, volume, seasonal variation and intended destination.
Relationships with qualified testing, repair and authorised handling partners suited to each stream.
A common costing method that includes collection, preparation, storage, transport, quality checks and material that cannot be sold.

categories.title: Subterranean cities

Full-size surface mock-ups and digital scenarios for accessibility, maintenance and everyday-life review without relying on an unproven habitat.
Qualified engineering and human-factors mentors alongside people who would use, clean, maintain and govern the proposed spaces.

sharedInfrastructure: A shared mission-assumption register with no implied launch or venue agreements
